If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted decline in early horizon (1–7 days) by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending downward, increase forecasted drop in mid-horizon (8–15 days) by 5–10% to reflect bearish momentum.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3 days, shift forecast peak earlier (by 1–3 days) and reduce peak magnitude by 10–15% to align with sentiment reversal.  
In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), apply a 3–5% downward bias to forecast to account for lagging market behavior.  
If sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending flat or slightly up, reduce forecasted rise in late horizon by 5–8% to prevent overoptimism.  
If sentiment is negative and price is trending up, reduce forecasted rise in mid-horizon by 10–15% to reflect sentiment-induced volatility suppression.
